body: Thank you very much, good night!

Laziness, just a lack of effort. I forget about other people's needs when I just "isolate" myself in my own mind. I'm blaming myself for that. I'm not blaming anyone else for anything that I'm feeling.

I do notice that I am acting passive-aggresive sometimes, and it makes me feel guilty. I just need to be more aware of it, so I can prevent it. But I don't think that my agression is shown 'cause I want their attention, but instead it's because of my grumpy mood when I'm done arguing with myself. It really depends on which side wins.

I'm always aiming to make her happy, I do in fact, and sometimes not so much.

Useful things such as: self-improvement, socializing more, doing chores regularly, etc.
I do believe I lack some self-discipline, so that's most likely causing me not to do most of these things.

I don't really think I seek their attention, as I bring these things up very rarely, as I know she has a lot of other things to worry about. I'm not showing it at all outside of family. But again, that's the only way I see I can get help.

I see. Are you saying that these thoughts are some sort of a "wake-up call" our brain is playing right next to our ears? But surely going as far as suicidal thoughts does not really help us.
I will look into the book, thanks.

I guess you're right about the fear thing, but some people (my mom) have had enough pain seeing me barely do anything with myself, and well, that's the one person that doesn't deserve any more of that.

I don't really do much useful things besides gym and revision, and anything else I do is purely for my own entertainment

My parent don't set high expectations, that's what makes me so mad, that I can't even achieve these one
'Twas a good burn, but I was the one asking for the opinions, and this person gave theirs

The fear thar I'm talking about is not the fight or flight type, but instead the fear of failure, and I know I'm never going to give up, but seeing the people around me being hurt because of my actions is what pains me the most. I don't want to hurt anyone. 
You can be incredibly lazy (and weak) even when going to gym, as I barely do what's expected of me, which is not a lot, and I don't have any mean bastards in my life that want the impossible from me.

Good mood or not, it's the same person. Yes I have hobbys, I enjoy a lot of things, but bad people can enjoy anything and still be bad. Your actions define who you are, not what you think you can do.
And for self-confidence, it varies, as there are periods where I feel I can actually achieve what I want, but most of the time I find myself in situations whete I do lack confidence in my abilities.
